question: Has the TDEC septic inspection process been initiated — with only 85 days to the October 5 start and a 70-day minimum TDEC lead time, there is essentially no scheduling buffer?
why_it_matters: TDEC contact must happen now or the start date slips; this is the longest single lead-time item on an addition per job-definition rules (septic_inspection_required fact).

question: Has the existing electrical service amperage been verified to support the new 100-amp subpanel without requiring a main service upgrade?
why_it_matters: Addition job-type rules mandate a pre-construction amperage check whenever a subpanel is in scope; discovering an upgrade need mid-project adds cost and delay (subpanel_scope fact).

question: Is a saddle detail or flashing tie-in methodology documented in the drawing set for where the new 3/12 gable roof meets the existing 6/12 roof?
why_it_matters: A 3/12-to-6/12 tie-in without a detail is a common leak origin; addition job-type rules also flag concealed structural conditions at this junction as a schedule-buffer risk (roof_tie_in_pitch_detail fact).

question: Has the roof framing method (trusses vs. stick rafter) been decided, given custom trusses carry a 28–42 day procurement lead time that must be triggered at structural sign-off?
why_it_matters: The decision is currently deferred in the scope; if trusses are chosen and the order is delayed, framing stalls — roof framing is the largest single cost section at $9,652 (roof_tie_in_pitch_detail fact).

question: Scope describes 'basement-level storage' but the foundation section specifies only footings and a 4" slab with no CMU or full-height foundation wall — how is the lower storage space being enclosed?
why_it_matters: If the lower level requires CMU stem walls or full foundation walls, the foundation scope and cost are understated in the current breakdown (job_scope_summary and scope.pdf:Foundation).

question: The breakdown's 'Existing Hall Bath Mod, Bedroom Remodel & Closeout' section shows a -$4,199.00 materials cost — is this an intentional salvage credit or a data-entry error?
why_it_matters: A negative section total of -$1,714.20 inflates the apparent overall margin; if it is an error, the true job total is higher and the 30% margin floor check may change (retrofit_section_present fact).

question: Have tile, fixture, and flooring selections been finalized by the customer before the October 5 demo start?
why_it_matters: TCR policy prohibits scheduling or starting demo without final material selections; the master bath custom tile shower and flooring are explicitly called out in scope with no selections on record (scope.pdf:Master Bathroom).

question: Breakdown CSV reports 789 sqft overall footprint while the scope describes a 30'x10' addition (300 sqft/floor, ~600 sqft two-story) — does the 789 include the existing bedroom remodel area or is there a scope-size discrepancy?
why_it_matters: If the footprint basis in the breakdown overestimates the addition, material quantities may be off; if it correctly includes the existing retrofit area, the breakdown basis is sound (breakdown_footprint_sqft fact).
